_note: Per-standard on-slide student activities for the Unit 1 TCAP deck. Each pairs to a real printable in the History Hack repo. Cornell Notes are confirmed to match the deck's standard mapping (lib/cornell-notes-data.ts). Worksheet hub: Teacher Tools > Worksheets.

US.01.title: Cause-and-Effect Web: Tying the Nation Together
US.01.prompt: Using the railroad map and the Golden Spike photo, list THREE effects of the Transcontinental Railroad on (a) settlers, (b) immigrant labor, and (c) American Indian nations. For each effect, mark whether it was a benefit or a cost — and to whom.
US.01.deliverable: Completed cause-effect web with at least 6 labeled effects.
US.01.worksheet: Cornell Notes — US.01: Transcontinental Railroad & Industrial Expansion (Teacher Tools › Worksheets › Cornell Notes)
US.01.differentiation: Entry: sentence stems provided. Honors: rank the three groups by net impact and defend the order.

US.02.title: Claim & Evidence: What Did the Policy Do?
US.02.prompt: Examine the Tom Torlino before/after photographs and the Dawes Act excerpt. In your own words, write what each policy CLAIMED to do and what it ACTUALLY did, citing one piece of evidence for each. Then take a position: was federal assimilation policy primarily about land, about culture, or both? Support your claim with evidence from today's sources.
US.02.deliverable: A claim-evidence-reasoning (CER) paragraph with at least two cited sources.
US.02.worksheet: Cornell Notes — US.02: Federal Policies Toward American Indians (Teacher Tools › Worksheets › Cornell Notes)
US.02.differentiation: Entry: T-chart (Claimed | Actually) instead of paragraph. Honors: evaluate the term “cultural genocide” — is it supported by the evidence? Why or why not?

US.03.title: Reading a Political Cartoon as Evidence
US.03.prompt: Analyze Thomas Nast's “Worse Than Slavery” cartoon and the Freedmen's Bureau image. Identify (1) the artist's point of view, (2) two symbols and their meaning, and (3) what the cartoon argues about why Reconstruction's protections collapsed.
US.03.deliverable: Annotated cartoon analysis with point-of-view statement.
US.03.worksheet: Cornell Notes — US.03: Reconstruction (Amendments, Freedmen's Bureau, End of Reconstruction)
US.03.differentiation: Entry: guided symbol list. Honors: compare Nast's view to the photo of the SC legislature — do the sources corroborate?

US.04.title: Machine Politics: Trade-Off Analysis
US.04.prompt: Using “The Bosses of the Senate” cartoon, list what a city political machine GAVE residents and what it TOOK. Then decide: why would voters keep electing a corrupt machine? Reach a group consensus and be ready to defend it.
US.04.deliverable: Give/Take T-chart plus a one-sentence group claim.
US.04.worksheet: Cornell Notes — US.04: Gilded Age Politics (Machines, Scandals & Civil Service Reform)
US.04.differentiation: Entry: provide 3 give/take examples to sort. Honors: connect to a modern trade-off between services and accountability.

US.05.title: Robber Baron or Captain of Industry?
US.05.prompt: Using the Carnegie portrait and the Standard Oil “Next!” cartoon, build the strongest case for ONE label — “robber baron” OR “captain of industry” — for a Gilded Age titan. Cite at least two specific actions as evidence.
US.05.deliverable: A position card with claim + two pieces of evidence.
US.05.worksheet: Cornell Notes — US.05: Inventions & Innovators of the Industrial Age
US.05.differentiation: Entry: evidence bank provided. Honors: argue the opposite label, then decide which case is stronger.

US.06.title: Mapping the Industrial City
US.06.prompt: Using the 1890 wage-earners and foreign-born maps, identify the regions where industry and immigration concentrated. Predict THREE problems a city would face when its population multiplies in 40 years, and THREE things it needs to grow.
US.06.differentiation: Entry: labeled map regions provided. Honors: explain the correlation between manufacturing density and foreign-born population.

US.07.title: Two Sides of Immigration
US.07.prompt: Examine Jacob Riis's “Five Cents a Spot” photograph and the Ellis Island inspection-room image. Write one sentence from the perspective of a new immigrant and one from a nativist worried about change. Then explain what Riis wanted viewers to FEEL and DO.
US.07.deliverable: Two perspective sentences + a photographer's-purpose statement.
US.07.differentiation: Entry: sentence stems for both perspectives. Honors: evaluate whether a staged photo is reliable evidence.
